issues.body: `is_well_formed_absolute_iri` only validates the scheme and rejects a small character blacklist. That is not sufficient to establish a well-formed RFC 3987 IRI as its contract claims. For example, `http://example.com/%ZZ` passes this predicate even though `%` must introduce two hexadecimal digits; component-specific invalid forms are likewise not checked. Because `expand.rs` now relies on this helper for JSON-LD datatype validation, authored malformed datatype IRIs can still expand successfully, contrary to the stated §5.1.2 step 15.5 behavior. The added test covers only a literal space and therefore does not expose the incomplete validator.
issues.fix_hint: Use a complete RFC 3987 IRI validator (or implement the required grammar, including valid percent-encoding and component constraints) rather than a blacklist. Add a regression test through the public expansion path for a malformed datatype such as `http://example.com/%ZZ`, asserting `InvalidTypedValue`, plus a nearby valid percent-encoded datatype case.
issues.title: The new well-formed IRI predicate accepts malformed IRIs

verdict.summary: The negative-test runner changes and exact error-code checks are well targeted, but the new datatype-IRI validator does not implement the well-formedness guarantee claimed by the code and required by the expansion rule. It still accepts malformed absolute IRIs, so the conformance fix is incomplete beyond the single space-containing fixture.
